name: TokenTracker
summary: Drop-in Python wrapper and CLI that logs LLM API calls to local SQLite and reports costs.
use_cases: see LLM spending by model and day
project future spend from recent usage
find spend spikes and cheaper-model savings
compare cost of workload across other models
features: set spending budgets and check them

usage_guide.open_hint: Run `tokentracker dashboard` to see your logged LLM spending.

features.title: Track LLM API costs automatically
steps: In your Python code, import the client from TokenTracker instead of the OpenAI package: `from tokentracker import OpenAI`.
Make API calls as usual; each call is logged to a local SQLite database.
Use `summary(days=30)` or `recent(limit=1)` from `tokentracker` to read back calls and costs.

features.title: View spending in a command-line dashboard
steps: Run `tokentracker dashboard` to see API calls and costs.

features.feature: set spending budgets and check them
features.title: Set spending budgets and check them
steps: Set a budget with `tokentracker budgets set monthly --limit <amount>`.
Run `tokentracker budgets check` to see spend against each budget.

linux.first_task: rm -f /tmp/tt_usage.db && TOKENTRACKER_DB=/tmp/tt_usage.db uv tool run --from toktally python /tmp/tt_track.py 2>&1

smoke_tests.observed_excerpt: dashboard Show a summary dashboard of your LLM spending.

smoke_tests.command: rm -f /tmp/tt_usage.db && TOKENTRACKER_DB=/tmp/tt_usage.db uv tool run --from toktally python /tmp/tt_track.py 2>&1

setup.command:
cat > /tmp/tt_stub.py <<'PY'
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        n = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(n) if n else b''
        try:
            data = json.loads(body or b'{}')
        except Exception:
            data = {}
        model = data.get('model', 'gpt-4o-mini')
        resp = {"id":"chatcmpl-test","object":"chat.completion","created":1700000000,"model":model,"choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Hello!"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":5,"total_tokens":15}}
        out = json.dumps(resp).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type','application/json')
        self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(out)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(out)
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1',8765), H).serve_forever()
PY
cat > /tmp/tt_track.py <<'PY'
from tokentracker import OpenAI, summary, recent
client = OpenAI(api_key="test-key", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1")
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}])
print("REPLY:", r.choices[0].message.content)
s = summary(days=30)
print(f"TRACKED calls={s['total_calls']} cost={s['total_cost_usd']}")
for c in recent(limit=1):
    print(f"RECENT model={c['model']} tokens={c['total_tokens']} cost={c['cost_usd']}")
PY

judge.observed: Help lists the dashboard command, the tracking script records one call with 15 tokens, and the dashboard displays that 1 API call with cost breakdowns.

features.feature: set spending budgets and check them

what_it_does.quote: Drop-in LLM cost tracker — change one import line, see where your money goes. Supports OpenAI, OpenRouter, Azure, Ollama.

who_it_is_for.quote: TokenTracker is for developers who want to know their LLM costs without adopting a platform.

troubleshooting_uninstall.quote: **Does this slow down my API calls?**

evidence.quote: change one import line, see where your money goes.
Set budgets and fail CI when you blow them
Project the current seven-day run rate
Find spend spikes, concentration, and cheaper-model opportunities
Reprice your actual token volume on other models
Nothing is ever sent to any external service.
every API call is tracked automatically
Define named spending limits once — a total cap, or one scoped to a model, endpoint, or tag — and check them all at a glance.
